messages:
talia: heads-up: scheduling a small powercap + fan-curve adjustment across a subset of az3 GPU racks to reduce thermal throttling during peak. window: Tue 2026-04-21 03:00-04:30 UTC. we'll do soft drains as a precaution, but aim for sub-1min host perturbations.

jyot: what exactly are we changing? will this touch dedicated racks?

talia: tweak: lower rack powercap by ~5% and apply a slightly more aggressive fan curve for 30 racks in az3-edge-slice-B. Dedicated/reserved racks excluded. this is low-risk but thermal changes can cause short re-registrations. fallback region: az1.

marta: previous runs caused KV cold starts. mitigation?

jyot: plan: pre-warm prefix/KV on standbys at T-40m (seed 0.85), enable continuous-batching fallback for 45m post-change. also suppress long synthetic evals for 2h.

kevin: cost note: if spillover sends ~50k tokens to hosted, delta ~= $575 (@ $0.0115/token). will confirm.

ops-bot: maintenance ticket created: MO-2640 https://redwood.atlassian/issue/MO-2640

talia: canary: 3 racks in eu-west3 at T-30m. abort if p99 latency increase > 0.4% or requeue rate > 0.7%.

therm-bot: recent telemetry: az3 racks have 3% of hosts hitting thermal headroom events in last 24h; fan speed often lags by ~6s. proposing this tweak reduces headroom events by ~60% in simulation.

marta: timeline (tentative):
- 02:20 pre-seed KV on warm standbys
- 02:30 apply fancurve + powercap to canary eu-west3 racks (3 racks)
- 02:50 validate + 10m buffer
- 03:05 begin az3 staggered cohorts (5 racks per 8min cohort)
- 04:15 final validation
- 04:30 close window
who's oncall?

jyot: oncall: marta, jyot. talia will run rollout. kevin on cost. deploy-bot will tag the rollout.

ops-bot: preflight checklist added to MO-2640: kvseed, canary perf check, autoscaler cap, comms posted, thermal monitor watch, rollback playbook attached.

talia: preflight commands (infra-runbook snippet):
```bash
# pre-seed KV
python infra/kvseed.py --pool az3-edge-slice-B --seed 0.85 --timeout 2400
# set autoscaler cap
kubectl patch hpa cluster-autoscaler -p '{"spec":{"maxSurge":0.12}}'
# apply fancurve/powercap via hwctl
infra/hwctl set-fancurve --racks az3-rack-[05..34] --profile aggressive-1
infra/hwctl set-powercap --racks az3-rack-[05..34] --percent 95
```

marta: note: do NOT disable autoscaling. last event where we suspended autoscaler caused heavy hosted fallback. keep maxSurge >=10%.

kevin: Posting updated cost delta to #finance at T-30m.

talia: rollback playbook (short):
```text
if p99_latency_delta > 0.4% or requeue_rate > 0.7% or thermal-errors_increase:
  - pause rollout
  - revert fancurve and powercap on last cohort
  - re-inject drained nodes
  - route traffic back to az1
  - open priority incident and escalate to hw vendor
```

therm-bot: automated perf check will run 5m after each cohort change: checks p50/p95/p99, requeue rates, thermal headroom. failing cohort auto-pauses rollout.

deploy-bot: scheduled reminder: MO-2640 will start Tue 2026-04-21 03:00 UTC. Canary automation triggers at T-30m.

marta: I'll publish a short customer advisory targeted to burst pool owners and lock autoscaler cap at T-20m. everyone else ok with this plan?

jyot: ok from netops side. i'll watch BGP-pref for az1 fallback and be ready to flip if needed.

talia: thanks all — we'll keep the window tight and abort on any sign of regression. :white_check_mark:
